premise.note: Act 3 ends with the half-in position: 2 shares of NVX at $21.00, $58.00 left in cash. Every dollar figure below is asserted against the fixture by server/tests/test_scenes.py.

act4.open.speaker: coach
lines: You own 2 shares of Novexa now. Let's let some days go by and see what happens.
I'll go quiet for a bit — just watch the price move.
act4.open.next: Don't worry, I'll jump back in the moment there's something worth talking about.

act4.drop5.speaker: coach
lines: Alright — it dipped.
Your 2 shares were worth $42.00. Right now they're worth $39.62.
act4.drop5.next: That's a paper loss — it isn't real until you decide it is. You've got three ways to go, and none of them is the wrong one.

respond.prompt: What do you want to do?

act4.chose.sell.speaker: coach
lines: Sold. The $2.38 is real now, and you've got $97.62 sitting safely in cash.
Some people will call that the scared choice. It's not — it's the choice that lets you sleep tonight, and a person who sleeps keeps investing tomorrow.
act4.chose.sell.next: Let's see what the market got up to after you left.

act4.chose.hold.speaker: coach
lines: You held on. Nothing's really changed except a number on a screen.
You still own the same 2 shares of the same company. Novexa didn't get worse this week — only the price did.
act4.chose.hold.next: Let's see if that was the right call.

act4.chose.more.speaker: coach
lines: You picked up 1 more at $19.81. You're at 3 shares now, averaging $20.60 each.
That also means more of your $100 is riding on this one company. Both things are true at once — more upside, more exposure.
act4.chose.more.next: Let's see how that plays out.

act4.resume.speaker: coach
lines: Okay, running again.
act4.resume.next: I'll pause it when it's worth pausing.

act4.deep.speaker: coach
lines: It kept sliding. Five more days, and Novexa is down a full ten percent from where you bought in.
If you'd held, that $42.00 is worth $37.80 today.
I'll be honest — this is the moment where most people sell and never come back.
act4.deep.next: I'm not going to tell you what to do here. But whatever you pick, I'll show you exactly what happened next.

respond.prompt: Same three choices. Still no wrong answer.

act4.compare.speaker: coach
lines: Right now, at the lowest point, those three choices are $2.73 apart.
Selling early looks like a smart move. Buying more looks like a mistake.
Hold that thought for a second.
act4.compare.next: Let's run it all the way to the end and see how it actually shakes out.

act4.recovery.speaker: coach
lines: Fifty-six days later, here's where things landed.
Sold: $97.62. Held: $110.50. Bought more: $116.94.
At the bottom those three were $2.73 apart. Now they're $19.32 apart — and the one that looked smartest is the one that ended up last.
act4.recovery.next: Selling at the low turned a dip you could have waited out into the only permanent loss on the board.

respond.label: So what do I take from that?

act4.lesson.speaker: coach
lines: Both versions of you who stayed in crossed $110 and won Vela her wager. The one who sold ended up below where she started.
Novexa was the same company the whole way through. The only thing that changed on the day you'd have sold was how it felt.
act4.lesson.next: That's the lesson: the dip was temporary, and the decision you make inside it is the part that lasts.

respond.prompt: Anything you're thinking that you'd like to jot down before we move on? This stays just between us.

act4.close.speaker: coach
lines: One more thing — and it's the part almost everyone tells me they don't know.
act4.close.next: I think you're about to prove that wrong.
